alignments.note: Construct אִישׁ realized by the substantival pronoun *He*; the relational expression of the chain goes to the rectum under rule 19.

The nomen rectum תּוֹכָחוֹת carries the ASV's recasting of the construct relation as the participial phrase *being often reproved*, with the copula rule 20 supplies for its predicate; headed on *reproved*, the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31). *often* renders the plural and is not added. The relative *that* is no part of this unit: it subordinates the finite clause whose verb is *hardeneth*, and a non-finite participial adjunct licenses no relative of its own.

Corrected. The Hiphil participle מַקְשֶׁה is an articleless attributive on אִישׁ that the ASV recasts as a relative clause, so the supplied *that* joins the attributive itself under rule 41 and the unit is discontinuous around the rectum's rendering under rule 25 — exactly as PRO.29.14 gives שׁוֹפֵט both *that* and *judgeth* around the interposed *faithfully*, and as PRO.29.5 and PRO.29.20 do with no interposed material. Headed on *hardeneth*, which realizes the lexeme (rule 24). The prior alignment gave *that* to תּוֹכָחוֹת; that reading is available only where no attributive participle stands to carry it, which is what PRO.29.4 is.
עֹרֶף carries no pronominal suffix, so the supplied possessive *his* answers to no morpheme (rule 18's closing sentence).
Niphal imperfect with its auxiliaries; headed on the lexical verb *destroyed* (rule 24). Discontinuous around *suddenly* under rule 25.
The resumptive *that* of *and that without remedy* answers to no morpheme; the waw already holds its *and* and the existential its *without* (rule 51's counting reasoning).
Existential אֵין rendered *without*; headed on the negation word (rule 50).

review_notes: The one change moves *that* from the rectum's unit to the attributive participle's, making PRO.29.1 read as PRO.29.5, PRO.29.14 and PRO.29.20 do under rule 41.

The competing reading, taken by the verse pass, gives *that being often reproved* whole to תּוֹכָחוֹת as the recast construct relation. It is the right reading of PRO.29.4, where no participle stands in the phrase; here the participle is what the English relative clause's finite verb renders, so the relative is the participle's.
